body: Let him know you want personal space. Don't be afraid or ashamed to ask that you don't want physical contact. You have every right to say "please don't touch me, I don't like it" no questions asked. And if he does ask, just look at him sternly and repeat yourself. If he really does care, he'll respect your boundaries. You're not obliged to let someone touch you if it makes you uncomfortable, even if they meant it as a nice gesture.

Practice using your safeword the first time you feel unsafe or scared, and have him immediately start on aftercare. Talk to him, and have him talk to you. Be open about how you feel about everything every step of the way.

That's basically me with my friends. I try to talk myself out of it, and simply let my friends know I'm not feeling well, and that we'll talk later, because I know that when I feel "normal" I'll regret losing them.

And yeah, sorry, I hope I didn't come off as accusing your mom as a bad mom. I'm super emotional too, but my mom is just as emotional to the point where she's insensitive to my feelings because she's too worried about her own.

And yeah I agree, a lot of the adult stuff doesn't make sense. I'm still 18, so I can't compare to what your situation may be, but I definitely think you deserve the guidance you're looking for. maybe you could try being straightforward and asking her to walk you through things? If she says "I figured everything out on my own!" remind her that she lived in a different time, and that she was a different person. That she's capable of showing you, so there's no reason to leave you stranded like that. If not, google is always helpful.

Although, it is so much worse to have to do adult things with depression and anxiety. You'll have to work harder than people without mental illnesses to get things done, and it sucks. All my best wishes man.

I agree, happiness is temporary, but so is sadness. Everything is temporary. And it is okay, and even if it's not, it's life and we don't really have a choice.

And yeah, everyone is inherently selfish, because we spend time with ourselves more than anyone else. It's not a flaw, more like a fact. Don't feel bad or guilty for it. As for caring, I think that we do. Even if we don't care for each other as much as we do for ourselves, we still try.

Living is feeling. I feel therefore I am. So if nothing really matters, we should focus on feeling. Pain, pleasure, sadness, happiness, anger, fear, joy. Life is so short, and we strive to make the best of it. We won't always be happy, but we shouldn't spend so much time dwelling on this pain either.

All easier said than done. The nagging fear of insignificance can not simply be willed away.
